newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: OIL COMPANIES TO PAY COLOMBIA ENVIRONMENTAL FINES.
newsitem.headline: OIL COMPANIES TO PAY COLOMBIA ENVIRONMENTAL FINES.

text.p: Colombia's Environment Ministry imposed a fine which includes a cash payment of 15 million pesos (about $13,000) on British Petroleum Co Plc, Triton Energy Corp and state oil company Ecopetrol for damage caused during the construction of a new pipeline, officials said on Tuesday.
Besides the cash payment, the fine includes investment in the planting and maintenance of of 148 acres (60 ha) of trees at the cost of 3 million pesos (about $2,700) per hectare.

The ministry statement said some crude had been spilled during construction and testing but did not specify how much. It also said some of the pipes had been mislaid in several stretches, causing a greater than expected environmental impact.
The three companies hit with the fine are part of a public- private sector consortium behind the $2 billion Ocensa pipeline, which was completed in June.
The 520 m) pipeline will pump crude from BP's Cusiana-Cupiagua field in Colombia's eastern plains to the lifting terminal at Covenas, on the Caribbean coast.
Ocensa estimates the pipeline will be pumping 450,000 barrels of crude per day (bpd) by the end of August and will reach maximum capacity of about 630,000 bpd by early next year.
